declaration.preface:
Sri All India Exports is steadfast in its commitment to maintaining the highest ethical standards across all aspects of our operations. As a prominent leader in the textile industry, we are dedicated to fostering an environment of integrity, transparency, and accountability. This Ethics Policy articulates our commitment to ethical behavior and outlines the framework for addressing key ethical issues, including corruption, conflict of interest, fraud, money laundering, anti-competitive practices, and information security.

Our goal is to ensure that all employees, stakeholders, and partners conduct business with honesty and respect for legal and ethical standards. This policy serves as a guide for maintaining ethical conduct, safeguarding the company’s reputation, and complying with legal requirements.
declaration.declaration: At Sri All India Exports, we uphold the highest standards of ethical behavior. We are committed to preventing and addressing unethical conduct and ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations. This policy reinforces our dedication to ethical practices and provides a clear framework for addressing potential ethical issues.
declaration.scope: This policy is exclusively applicable to the operations of Sri All India Exports, covering all employees, workers, subcontractors, and other stakeholders directly affiliated with our site.

Corruption: Develop and roll out a comprehensive anti-corruption training program for all new employees. For example, employees will participate in a workshop on recognizing and preventing bribery and other forms of corruption within their first month of employment.
Create a dedicated, confidential channel for reporting corruption, and ensure all employees are aware of and can use this system without fear of retaliation.
Establish a confidential reporting system where employees can anonymously report suspected corruption. For instance, set up an online portal and a hotline dedicated to reporting unethical behavior.
Conflict of Interest: Create a formal process for employees to disclose potential conflicts of interest. For example, employees will be required to fill out a conflict-of-interest declaration form when they join the company and annually thereafter.
Develop a system for reviewing disclosed conflicts of interest. For instance, establish a committee that meets quarterly to assess and manage any disclosed conflicts.

Establish a transparent process for decision-making that includes checks to identify and mitigate conflicts of interest. For example, decisions on promotions or major contracts will involve a review by a committee to ensure impartiality.
Fraud: Implement internal controls to prevent fraud. For example, introduce a new verification process for financial transactions to detect any anomalies.
Create secure channels for reporting suspected fraud. For instance, establish a confidential email and phone line where employees can report fraud anonymously.
Organize workshops to raise awareness about fraud and its prevention. Employees will participate in quarterly workshops that cover different aspects of fraud prevention.
Money Laundering: Implement a monitoring system to detect potential money laundering activities. For instance, use software to flag unusual transactions for further investigation.
Offer training on anti-money laundering practices to all employees. Host bi-annual training sessions that include case studies and scenarios related to money laundering.

Maintain detailed records of all transactions and customer interactions to support auditing and regulatory compliance. For example, keep transaction records and customer identification information for a specified period.
Anti-Competitive Practices: Develop and implement policies to prevent anti-competitive practices. For example, draft a policy that prohibits any form of price-fixing or market manipulation.
Conduct reviews of market conduct to ensure compliance with competition laws. For instance, perform semi-annual audits of pricing and market practices.
Offer training on competition laws and fair market practices. Employees will attend an annual training session focusing on the importance of fair competition.
Information Security: Enhance information security by updating data protection measures. For example, introduce new encryption protocols and secure access controls.
Provide regular training on information security. Employees will participate in bi-annual training sessions covering topics such as data protection and response to security incidents.
Develop an incident response plan and test it regularly. For example, conduct simulations of data breaches to refine the response plan and improve preparedness.
Use encryption for protecting data. For instance, encrypt customer data both when stored and during transmission to prevent unauthorized access.

responsibilities.duty: Oversees implementation of the Ethics Policy, ensures compliance with ethical standards and codes of conduct, and maintains reporting mechanisms.
Provides oversight to ensure the Ethics Policy aligns with the company’s values, integrity, and governance strategy.
Act as role models, promote ethical behavior in their teams, and serve as the first point of contact for ethical concerns.
Receive regular training on ethical responsibilities, follow the company’s Code of Conduct, and are encouraged to report unethical practices without fear of retaliation.

policy.monitoring:
Conduct monthly evaluations of ethics performance indicators, including incidents of corruption, conflicts of interest, and information security breaches.

Utilize data collection methods such as surveys and reporting systems to ensure accurate and real-time data.

Publish a detailed annual ethics report outlining our practices, achievements, challenges, and future goals.

Include case studies and success stories, such as improvements in fraud prevention or information security.

Have the report independently audited to ensure accuracy and credibility.

Document and report on feedback received through surveys and forums, including participant numbers, key themes, and actions taken in response.

Share feedback trends and improvement actions with employees to maintain transparency and engagement.

Conduct and report on annual audits of supplier ethics practices, including compliance with our policies and any corrective actions taken.

Include information on supplier adherence to our ethical standards and areas identified for improvement.

Provide reports on stakeholder engagement activities, including meetings, consultations, and feedback received.

Summarize the outcomes of these engagements and how they have influenced our ethics practices and policies.

Establish a system for reporting and addressing any ethics-related incidents or concerns.

Provide monthly summaries of incidents, including root cause analysis, corrective actions taken, and any improvements implemented.
policy.reviewMechanism: The Human Resources Office is responsible for the implementation, oversight, and review of this policy. This policy will be reviewed every year, and any updates will be communicated as necessary.
